   235	export function rotateJournal(root, kind, io) {

   239	/**
   240	 * Lock-context rotation: caller holds the lock and passes its fencing token.
   241	 * @param {string} root @param {'finalize'|'takeover'|'receive'} kind @param {any} io @param {string} token
   242	 * @returns {string} the history stem for this rotation
   243	 */
   244	export function rotateJournalIn(root, kind, io, token) {
   245	  const p = bundlePaths(root);
   246	  return guardedWrite(root, io, token, () => {
   247	    assertHandoffTreeSafe(root, io);
   248	    ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
   249	    const startedAt = io.now();
   250	    const stem = `${tsForFile(startedAt)}.${kind}`;
   251	    const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, p.snapshot);
   252	    const seq = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.journalSeq === 'number' ? snap.value.journalSeq : 0;
   253	
   254	    atomicWriteJson(io.fs, markerPath(p), { kind, startedAt, seq });
   255	    ensureDir(io.fs, p.historyDir);
   256	
   257	    if (io.fs.existsSync(p.snapshot)) {
   258	      // Atomic freeze (gate-2 minor 16): tmp+rename, so a crash mid-copy can
   259	      // never leave a partial history snapshot that recovery would trust.
   260	      atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.json`, io.fs.readFileSync(p.snapshot, 'utf8'));
   261	    } else {
   262	      atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.json`, '');
   263	    }
   264	    if (io.fs.existsSync(p.journal)) {
   265	      io.fs.renameSync(p.journal, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.ndjson`);
   266	    } else {
   267	      atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.ndjson`, '');
   268	    }
   269	    atomicWriteText(io.fs, p.journal, '');
   270	
   271	    // Retention: newest RETAIN_PER_KIND per kind (ISO-derived stems sort by time).
   272	    const freezes = io.fs
   273	      .readdirSync(p.historyDir)
   274	      .filter((/** @type {string} */ n) => n.endsWith(`.${kind}.json`))
   275	      .sort();

   277	      const oldest = /** @type {string} */ (freezes.shift());
   278	      const oldStem = oldest.slice(0, -'.json'.length);
   279	      for (const suffix of ['.json', '.ndjson']) {
   280	        try {
   281	          io.fs.unlinkSync(`${p.historyDir}/${oldStem}${suffix}`);
   282	        } catch {

     1	/**
     2	 * Loop failover orchestration — what the supervisor does when a child dies.
     3	 * Classifies the death via the signature table, then takes exactly one path:
     4	 * retry-once-then-park (generic failures), entry-level re-resolve
     5	 * (model-unavailable — the platform survives its dead model), or the
     6	 * usage-limit transaction: checkpoint the loop position INTO the bundle,
     7	 * seal, and receive onto the resolver's pick with one bounded stale retry.
     8	 * Writes NOTHING under .handoff/loop/ — the supervisor applies the returned
     9	 * decision to loop state afterward. Plan:
    10	 * docs/plans/2026-07-18-goal-loop-worktree-pipeline.md §"Limit failover" +
    11	 * §"Model-level failover".
    12	 */
    13	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
    14	import { join, dirname } from 'node:path';
    15	import { loadSignatures } from '../detect/signatures.mjs';
    16	import { classify } from '../detect/classifier.mjs';
    17	import { resolveRoles } from '../roles/resolve.mjs';
    18	import { loadBundle } from '../bundle/store.mjs';
    19	import { snapshot as gitSnapshot } from '../git/snapshot.mjs';
    20	import { prepare, commit } from '../receive/txn.mjs';
    21	import { cmdCheckpoint } from '../commands/checkpoint.mjs';
    22	import { cmdFinalize } from '../commands/finalize.mjs';
    23	
    24	const BUILTIN_SIGNATURES = join(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), '..', '..', 'data', 'signatures.v1.json');
    25	
    26	/**
    27	 * @param {{
    28	 *   root: string, io: any, config: any, role: string,
    29	 *   assignment: {platform: string, role?: string, model: string, effort?: string | null, mode?: string},
    30	 *   transcript: string, exitCode: number, sessionHint: string,
    31	 *   probes?: any, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>,
    32	 *   attempt: number, loopState?: any, degradedOpen?: boolean,
    33	 * }} input
    34	 * @returns {Promise<
    35	 *   | {action: 'retry', class: string, attempt: number}
    36	 *   | {action: 'park', class: string, reason: string, resumeAt?: string}
    37	 *   | {action: 'relaunch', class: string, assignment: any, avoidEntries?: any[], prompt?: string}
    38	 * >}
    39	 */
    40	export async function runFailover(input) {
    41	  const { root, io, config, role, assignment, sessionHint } = input;
    42	  const avoid = input.avoid ?? [];
    43	  const avoidEntries = input.avoidEntries ?? [];
    44	
    45	  // Classification is TABLE-driven — the same loader/classifier as `baton
    46	  // detect`, so overlay/fixture signatures are honored, never hardcoded.
    47	  const table = loadSignatures({ builtinPath: BUILTIN_SIGNATURES }, io);
    48	  const verdict = classify({ text: input.transcript, exitCode: input.exitCode, platform: assignment.platform, table });
    49	
    50	  // Model-level failure: the platform is fine, one model is dead. Avoid the
    51	  // exact {platform, model} tuple and re-resolve — no seal, no receive.
    52	  if (verdict.class === 'model-unavailable') {
    53	    const nextAvoidEntries = [...avoidEntries, { platform: assignment.platform, model: assignment.model }];
    54	    const resolved = resolveRoles({ config, to: assignment.platform, avoid, avoidEntries: nextAvoidEntries, probes: input.probes ?? null });
    55	    const next = resolved.assignments[role];
    56	    if (!next || next.mode === 'unavailable') {
    57	      return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `no eligible chain entry left for role '${role}' after avoiding ${assignment.platform}/${assignment.model}` };
    58	    }
    59	    return { action: 'relaunch', class: verdict.class, assignment: next, avoidEntries: nextAvoidEntries };
    60	  }
    61	
    62	  // Anything that is not a usage-limit death is a child failure, not a
    63	  // platform death: retry once, then park. Never a seal or receive.
    64	  if (verdict.class !== 'usage-limit') {
    65	    if (input.attempt <= 1) return { action: 'retry', class: verdict.class, attempt: input.attempt };
    66	    return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `child failed twice (${verdict.class}) — parked for operator review` };
    67	  }
    68	
    69	  // ---- Usage-limit: the exact transaction (plan steps 3–8). ----------------
    70	  const { bundle } = loadBundle(root, io);
    71	  const originPlatform = bundle?.origin?.platform ?? assignment.platform;
    72	
    73	  // (3) Checkpoint the loop position INTO the bundle under the supervisor
    74	  // session BEFORE any seal, so the frozen seal carries it.
    75	  if (input.loopState !== undefined) {
    76	    const checkpointIo = {
    77	      ...io,
    78	      stdin: JSON.stringify({
    79	        schema: 'baton/event@1',
    80	        events: [{ type: 'decision', payload: { summary: `loop position at limit death: ${JSON.stringify(input.loopState)}` } }],
    81	      }),
    82	    };
    83	    await cmdCheckpoint(['--platform', originPlatform, '--session', sessionHint, '--root', root], checkpointIo);
    84	  }
    85	
    86	  // (4) Seal — unless the caller knows a clean seal is impossible
    87	  // (degradedOpen: a prior death left the bundle unsealed; receive's
    88	  // degraded-open path compensates), or the bundle is already sealed.
    89	  const alreadySealed = bundle?.handoff?.status === 'sealed';
    90	  if (input.degradedOpen !== true && !alreadySealed) {
    91	    await cmdFinalize(['--reason', 'usage-limit death during a supervised loop run', '--reason-class', 'usage-limit', '--root', root], io);
    92	  }
    93	
    94	  // (7, ordered before receive because receive needs the target) — resolver
    95	  // pick with the dead origin platform avoided.
    96	  const relaunchAvoid = avoid.includes(assignment.platform) ? avoid : [...avoid, assignment.platform];
    97	  const resolved = resolveRoles({ config, to: assignment.platform, avoid: relaunchAvoid, avoidEntries, probes: input.probes ?? null });
    98	  const target = resolved.assignments[role];
    99	  if (!target || target.mode === 'unavailable') {
   100	    return {
   101	      action: 'park',
   102	      class: verdict.class,
   103	      reason: `every platform is avoided or unavailable for role '${role}' — parked with a resume hint`,
   104	      ...(verdict.resetHint ? { resumeAt: verdict.resetHint } : {}),
   105	    };
   106	  }
   107	
   108	  // (5–6) Receive prepare+commit back-to-back with IDENTICAL intake and the
   109	  // supervisor session hint. Git is re-derived fresh for each phase (exactly
   110	  // as the CLI does), so real drift inside the window stales the token; ONE
   111	  // automatic re-prepare retry, then park. No .handoff/loop writes anywhere.
   112	  const receiveOpts = (/** @type {any} */ git) => ({
   113	    platform: target.platform,
   114	    origin: 'unknown', // defaults from the sealed bundle's recorded origin
   115	    reason: 'unspecified', // defaults from the sealed reason
   116	    reasonClass: 'usage-limit',
   117	    gitSnapshot: git,
   118	    probes: input.probes ?? null,
   119	    sessionHint,
   120	    sessionUnstable: false,
   121	  });
   122	
   123	  /** @type {string} */
   124	  let prompt = '';
   125	  let lastError = null;
   126	  for (let window = 1; window <= 2; window += 1) {
   127	    const prepGit = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   128	    const prepared = prepare(root, receiveOpts(prepGit), io);
   129	    prompt = prepared.prompt;
   130	    const commitGit = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   131	    try {
   132	      commit(root, prepared.token, receiveOpts(commitGit), io);
   133	      lastError = null;
   134	      break;
   135	    } catch (err) {
   136	      lastError = err;
   137	    }
   138	  }
   139	  if (lastError !== null) {
   140	    const msg = /** @type {any} */ (lastError)?.message ?? String(lastError);
   141	    return { action: 'park', class: verdict.class, reason: `receive commit stayed stale after one re-prepare retry — ${msg}` };
   142	  }
   143	
   144	  // (8) Relaunch on the adopted platform with the resume prompt.
   145	  return {
   146	    action: 'relaunch',
   147	    class: verdict.class,
   148	    assignment: target,
   149	    avoidEntries,
   150	    prompt,
   151	  };
   152	}

   144	function gitExec(headForCall) {

   146	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
   147	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));

   149	    if (key === 'rev-parse HEAD') {
   150	      headCalls += 1;
   151	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: headForCall(headCalls) + '\n', stderr: '' });
   152	    }
   153	    const out = key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
   154	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
   155	  };
   156	  fn.headCalls = () => headCalls;
   157	  return fn;

    25	 * Opt-in transcript-tail capture (gate-2 fix 10). Returns the bounded,
    26	 * redacted tail or null when the gate is closed: config off (the default),
    27	 * not a PreCompact payload, no usable transcript_path, or an unreadable /
    28	 * symlinked file. The path comes from an untrusted hook payload — it is read
    29	 * only under explicit opt-in, must lstat as a regular file, and its content
    30	 * passes the secret-redaction filter before storage.
    31	 * @param {string} root @param {any} raw parsed hook payload @param {any} io
    32	 * @returns {string | null}
    33	 */
    34	function captureTranscriptTail(root, raw, io) {
    35	  const cfg = safeReadJson(io.fs, `${root}/baton.config.json`);
    36	  if (!cfg.ok || cfg.value?.capture?.transcriptTail !== true) return null;
    37	
    38	  const eventName = raw && typeof raw === 'object' ? (raw.hook_event_name ?? raw.event) : null;
    39	  if (typeof eventName !== 'string' || !/precompact/i.test(eventName)) return null;
    40	  const path = raw.transcript_path;
    41	  if (typeof path !== 'string' || path.length === 0) return null;
    42	
    43	  try {
    44	    if (!io.fs.lstatSync(path).isFile()) return null;
    45	    // Allowlist the transcript path (gate-2 iter-2 m1): the payload is
    46	    // untrusted, so its resolved realpath must sit under the repo root, the
    47	    // user's ~/.claude tree (where Claude Code actually writes transcripts),
    48	    // or a configured capture.transcriptDir — never an arbitrary readable file.
    49	    const fileReal = io.fs.realpathSync(path);
    50	    // On POSIX a backslash is a LEGAL filename character, not a separator, so
    51	    // normalizing '\\'→'/' in the containment check (isContained) could make an
    52	    // out-of-tree sibling like '/repo\\evil/f' appear contained (iter-4 I9).
    53	    // The transcript path is the one fully-untrusted path that reaches
    54	    // containment, so refuse a backslash-bearing realpath off Windows.
    55	    if (io.platform !== 'win32' && String(fileReal).includes('\\')) return null;
    56	    /** @type {string[]} */
    57	    const allowed = [root];
    58	    const home = io.env?.HOME;
    59	    if (typeof home === 'string' && home.length > 0) allowed.push(`${home}/.claude`);
    60	    const dir = cfg.value?.capture?.transcriptDir;
    61	    if (typeof dir === 'string' && dir.length > 0) allowed.push(dir);
    62	    const under = (/** @type {string} */ base) => {
    63	      let baseReal;
    64	      try {
    65	        baseReal = io.fs.realpathSync(base);
    66	      } catch {
    67	        baseReal = base;
    68	      }
    69	      // Compare on normalized forward-slash spellings (iter-3 F9): raw Windows
    70	      // backslash realpaths never satisfy a forward-slash containment, so
    71	      // opt-in capture would silently never fire.
    72	      return isContained(baseReal, fileReal);
    73	    };
    74	    if (!allowed.some(under)) return null;
    75	
    76	    const text = io.fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
    77	    const lines = text.split('\n').filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l.trim() !== '');
    78	    let tail = lines.slice(-TAIL_MESSAGES).join('\n');
    79	    if (Buffer.byteLength(tail) > TAIL_BYTES) {
    80	      tail = Buffer.from(tail).subarray(-TAIL_BYTES).toString('utf8');
    81	    }
    82	    return redactSecrets(tail);
    83	  } catch {
    84	    return null; // unreadable transcript is never a checkpoint failure
    85	  }
    86	}

    88	/** Event-shaped: an object carrying a string `type`. */
    89	const isEventShaped = (/** @type {any} */ v) => v !== null && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) && typeof v.type === 'string';
    90	
    91	/**
    92	 * Tolerant stdin parse (live /baton:handoff failure: a model sent one event
    93	 * per line and the whole narrative checkpoint silently failed). Accept the
    94	 * canonical single JSON value, a bare array of events, or NDJSON where every
    95	 * line is an event object or a {schema, events} wrapper. All-or-nothing: one
    96	 * non-event element fails the whole parse — never a partial apply.
    97	 * @param {string} text @returns {{ok: true, raw: any} | {ok: false, why?: string}}
    98	 */
    99	function parseStdin(text) {
   100	  let single;
   101	  let singleOk = false;
   102	  try {
   103	    single = JSON.parse(text);
   104	    singleOk = true;
   105	  } catch {
   106	    singleOk = false;
   107	  }
   108	  if (singleOk) {
   109	    if (Array.isArray(single)) {
   110	      return single.every(isEventShaped) ? { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: single } } : { ok: false };
   111	    }
   112	    // A closest-miss of the documented wrapper — an events array whose schema
   113	    // key is missing or wrong — must ERROR, never silently degrade to a junk
   114	    // note with ok:true (the model cannot self-correct from a success
   115	    // envelope while its narrative was discarded).
   116	    if (single !== null && typeof single === 'object' && Array.isArray(single.events) && single.schema !== 'baton/event@1') {
   117	      return { ok: false, why: `stdin carries an events array but schema is ${single.schema === undefined ? 'missing' : JSON.stringify(single.schema)} — use {"schema":"baton/event@1","events":[…]}` };
   118	    }
   119	    // A single bare event object (string `type`, none of the raw-hook payload
   120	    // markers) is one of the two most likely readings of "pipe events on
   121	    // stdin" — accept it as that event instead of degrading it to a junk note.
   122	    if (
   123	      isEventShaped(single) &&
   124	      single.schema === undefined &&
   125	      !('hook_event_name' in single) &&
   126	      !('session_id' in single) &&
   127	      !('event' in single)
   128	    ) {
   129	      return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events: [single] } };
   130	    }
   131	    return { ok: true, raw: single };
   132	  }
   133	  const lines = text.split('\n').map((l) => l.trim()).filter((l) => l !== '');
   134	  if (lines.length === 0) return { ok: false };
   135	  /** @type {any[]} */
   136	  const events = [];
   137	  for (const line of lines) {
   138	    let v;
   139	    try {
   140	      v = JSON.parse(line);
   141	    } catch {
   142	      return { ok: false };
   143	    }
   144	    if (v && typeof v === 'object' && v.schema === 'baton/event@1' && Array.isArray(v.events)) {
   145	      if (!v.events.every(isEventShaped)) return { ok: false };
   146	      events.push(...v.events);
   147	    } else if (isEventShaped(v)) {
   148	      events.push(v);
   149	    } else {
   150	      return { ok: false };
   151	    }
   152	  }
   153	  return { ok: true, raw: { schema: 'baton/event@1', events } };
   154	}

   156	/**
   157	 * `baton checkpoint` — mechanical checkpoint from a hook payload on stdin.
   158	 * Hook-safety rule: exit 0 on every soft failure so a checkpoint can never
   159	 * break the host harness; `--strict` opts into hard failures (CI).
   160	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io
   161	 * @returns {Promise<number>}
   162	 */
   163	export async function cmdCheckpoint(args, io) {
   164	  if (isSupervisedChild(io)) return 0;
   165	  const parsed = parseFlagsStrict(args, { platform: 'string', model: 'string', trigger: 'string', debounce: 'string', session: 'string', strict: 'boolean', 'take-over': 'boolean' });
   166	  if (parsed.error !== undefined) return usageError(io, parsed.flags, 'checkpoint', parsed.error);
   167	  const flags = parsed.flags;
   168	  const strict = flags.strict === true;
   169	  const platform = typeof flags.platform === 'string' ? flags.platform : null;
   170	  if (!platform) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', '--platform <claude-code|codex|cursor> is required');
   171	  const pErr = platformError(platform);
   172	  if (pErr) return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', pErr);
   173	  // A supervisor passing --session must never silently fall back to
   174	  // payload-derived identity: an empty value is a hard usage error.
   175	  if (flags.session === '') return usageError(io, flags, 'checkpoint', '--session must be a non-empty session hint (it cannot be empty)');
   176	
   177	  try {
   178	    return await run(flags, platform, io);
   179	  } catch (err) {

   181	    if (flags.json) emitEnvelope(io, { ok: false, error: { code: 'checkpoint-failed', msg } });
   182	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: ${msg}\n`);
   183	    return strict ? 1 : 0;
   184	  }
   185	}

     2	 * Pure, explainable role resolution over the committed matrix. Every decision

     5	 * @param {{config: any, to: string, avoid?: string[], avoidEntries?: Array<{platform: string, model: string}>, nativeOnly?: boolean, probes?: Record<string, {capability: string, outcome: string}> | null}} input
     6	 * @returns {{assignments: Record<string, any>, notes: string[]}}
     7	 */
     8	export function resolveRoles({ config, to, avoid = [], avoidEntries = [], nativeOnly = false, probes = null }) {
     9	  /** @type {string[]} */
    10	  const notes = [];
    11	
    12	  /**
    13	   * The eligibility verdict for a platform, or null when eligible.
    14	   * @param {string} platform @returns {string | null}
    15	   */
    16	  function skipReason(platform) {
    17	    if (avoid.includes(platform)) return 'avoided';
    18	    if (!(platform in (config.platforms ?? {}))) return 'unknown-platform';
    19	    if (config.platforms[platform]?.enabled === false) return 'disabled';
    20	    if (probes && probes[platform]) {
    21	      const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    22	      if (outcome === 'rate-limited') return 'rate-limited';
    23	      if (capability === 'not-installed') return 'not-installed';
    24	      // 'installed' means installation was PROVEN but the probe was capped there
    25	      // (capOnSuccess) — authentication is UNVERIFIED, not verified-failed. Only
    26	      // a probe that ran and did NOT succeed (outcome !== 'ok') is a verified
    27	      // auth/reachability failure worth skipping; a capped success stays
    28	      // selectable and is flagged degraded below (iter-3 F1, plan §Role matrix).
    29	      if (capability === 'installed' && outcome !== 'ok') return 'unauthenticated';
    30	    }
    31	    return null;
    32	  }
    33	
    34	  // A selection is degraded when its availability is UNVERIFIED (gate-2 iter-2
    35	  // M3, iter-3 F1): with no probe cache at all, resolution is offline and EVERY
    36	  // selection is degraded (plan: "Offline resolution always succeeds, flagged
    37	  // degraded"); with a partial cache, platforms the cache is missing are; and a
    38	  // platform probed only to 'installed' (auth unverified, e.g. a --version
    39	  // success) is degraded even though it stays selectable.
    40	  /** @param {string} platform */
    41	  const probeUnverified = (platform) => {
    42	    if (probes == null || !probes[platform]) return true;
    43	    const { capability, outcome } = probes[platform];
    44	    // Degraded when ANY required dimension is unverified: a capped 'installed'
    45	    // (auth never confirmed) OR a non-ok outcome (iter-4 I6) — a selectable
    46	    // platform whose last probe ERRORED or TIMED OUT is presented as
    47	    // reachability-verified otherwise, which is exactly the silent-degradation
    48	    // the plan's degraded flag exists to surface. (rate-limited is skipped, not
    49	    // selected, so it never reaches here.)
    50	    return capability === 'installed' || outcome !== 'ok';
    51	  };
    52	
    53	  // Entry-level avoidance (plan §Model-level failover): a specific
    54	  // {platform, model} tuple is dead (e.g. account-tier rejected) while its
    55	  // platform stays usable. Matching is on model IDENTITY — an @effort suffix
    56	  // on either side is ignored — and requires BOTH dimensions, so the same
    57	  // model name on another platform is never caught.
    58	  /** @param {any} m */
    59	  const baseModel = (m) => (typeof m === 'string' ? m.split('@')[0] : m);
    60	  /** @param {string} platform @param {string} model */
    61	  const entryAvoided = (platform, model) =>

    71

    73	      const entry = chain[i];
    74	      if (nativeOnly && entry.platform !== to) {
    75	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'non-native' });
    76	        continue;
    77	      }
    78	      const why = skipReason(entry.platform);
    79	      if (why) {
    80	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why });
    81	        continue;
    82	      }
    83	      // After skipReason so a dual match keeps the platform-level label.
    84	      if (entryAvoided(entry.platform, entry.model)) {
    85	        skipped.push({ chainIndex: i, platform: entry.platform, model: entry.model, why: 'avoided-entry' });
    86	        continue;
    87	      }
    88	      assignment = {
    89	        platform: entry.platform,
    90	        model: entry.model,
    91	        effort: entry.effort ?? null,
    92	        mode: entry.platform === to ? 'native' : 'delegated',
    93	        chainIndex: i,
    94	        skipped,
    95	      };
    96	      if (probeUnverified(entry.platform)) assignment.degraded = true;
    97	      break;
    98	    }
    99	
   100	    if (!assignment && nativeOnly) {
   101	      // Forced-default is only valid when the destination itself is eligible.
   102	      const whyTo = skipReason(to);
   103	      const model = config.defaults?.[to];
   104	      if (!whyTo && typeof model === 'string') {
   105	        assignment = { platform: to, model, effort: null, mode: 'forced-default', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   106	        if (probeUnverified(to)) assignment.degraded = true;
   107	      }
   108	    }
   109	
   110	    if (!assignment) {
   111	      assignment = { platform: null, model: null, effort: null, mode: 'unavailable', chainIndex: null, skipped };
   112	    }
   113	    assignments[role] = assignment;
   114	  }
   115	
   116	  return { assignments, notes };
   117	}

    27	/**
    28	 * Repo-root discovery (plan §Root discovery): `--root` wins; else the nearest
    29	 * ancestor of io.cwd carrying `.handoff/` or `baton.config.json`; else the
    30	 * nearest ancestor carrying `.git` (the repo toplevel — and a boundary the
    31	 * walk never crosses, so a nested repo resolves to itself); else io.cwd.
    32	 * @param {any} io @param {Record<string, string | boolean>} flags
    33	 * @returns {string}
    34	 */
    35	export function resolveRoot(io, flags) {
    36	  if (typeof flags.root === 'string' && flags.root.length > 0) return flags.root;
    37	  // Normalize separators up front (gate-2 iter-2 M2): a Windows cwd arrives
    38	  // backslash-separated, but Node fs accepts forward slashes, so the ascent
    39	  // and the marker checks work in one forward-slash space. The last separator
    40	  // is either kind; the loop stops at a drive/UNC or filesystem root.
    41	  const start = normSep(io.cwd);
    42	  let dir = start;
    43	  while (true) {
    44	    try {
    45	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.handoff')) || io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, 'baton.config.json'))) return dir;
    46	      if (io.fs.existsSync(joinNorm(dir, '.git'))) return dir; // repo toplevel; never walk past a .git boundary
    47	    } catch {
    48	      break;
    49	    }
    50	    const cut = dir.lastIndexOf('/');
    51	    if (cut < 0) break;
    52	    const parent = cut === 0 ? '/' : dir.slice(0, cut);
    53	    // At a drive-relative ceiling ("C:") examine the drive ROOT ("C:/") once —
    54	    // a repo can live directly at C:/ (iter-3 F6) — then stop.
    55	    if (/^[A-Za-z]:$/.test(parent)) {
    56	      const driveRoot = `${parent}/`;
    57	      if (driveRoot !== dir) {
    58	        dir = driveRoot;
    59	        continue;
    60	      }
    61	      break;
    62	    }
    63	    if (parent === dir) break;
    64	    dir = parent;
    65	  }
    66	  return start;
    67	}

    99	/**
   100	 * Strict flag parser (surface-audit fold; docs/design/core.md §tooling always
   101	 * specified strict parsing). spec maps each flag name to 'string' | 'boolean';
   102	 * `json` and `root` are implied common flags. Errors — unknown flag, stray
   103	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
   104	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token
   105	 * flip SAFETY flags off (checkpoint/doctor --strict, remap --native-only,
   106	 * receive --print-prompt all read fail-dangerous exit 0).
   107	 * @param {string[]} args
   108	 * @param {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} spec
   109	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, error?: string}}
   110	 */
   111	export function parseFlagsStrict(args, spec) {
   112	  /** @type {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} */
   113	  const full = { json: 'boolean', root: 'string', ...spec };
   114	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   115	  const flags = {};
   116	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   117	    const a = args[i];
   118	    if (!a.startsWith('--')) return { flags, error: `unexpected argument '${a}' — flags are --name [value]` };
   119	    const key = a.slice(2);
   120	    const kind = full[key];
   121	    if (kind === undefined) return { flags, error: `unknown flag --${key}` };
   122	    if (kind === 'boolean') {
   123	      // A following token that is not a flag would have been this flag's
   124	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.
   125	      const next = args[i + 1];
   126	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   127	        return { flags, error: `unexpected token '${next}' after --${key} (a bare flag takes no value)` };
   128	      }
   129	      flags[key] = true;
   130	      continue;
   131	    }
   132	    const next = args[i + 1];
   133	    // A string flag consumes the next token unless it is itself a KNOWN flag
   134	    // (so `--commit --origin x` errors instead of eating '--origin').
   135	    if (next === undefined || (next.startsWith('--') && full[next.slice(2)] !== undefined)) {
   136	      return { flags, error: `--${key} requires a value` };
   137	    }
   138	    flags[key] = next;
   139	    i += 1;
   140	  }
   141	  return { flags };
   142	}
   143	
   144	/**
   145	 * Minimal flag parser: `--key value` pairs (value = next token not starting
   146	 * with --), bare `--key` booleans, positionals collected in order.
   147	 * @param {string[]} args
   148	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, positionals: string[]}}
   149	 */
   150	export function parseFlags(args) {
   151	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
   152	  const flags = {};
   153	  /** @type {string[]} */
   154	  const positionals = [];
   155	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
   156	    const a = args[i];
   157	    if (a.startsWith('--')) {
   158	      const key = a.slice(2);
   159	      const next = args[i + 1];
   160	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
   161	        flags[key] = next;
   162	        i += 1;
   163	      } else {
   164	        flags[key] = true;
   165	      }
   166	    } else {
   167	      positionals.push(a);
   168	    }
   169	  }
   170	  return { flags, positionals };
   171	}

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:2962:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6325:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-01/raw-output.txt:348:    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:2993:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6696:reviews/2026-07-12-gate-2-final/reviewer-a/iteration-05/raw-output.txt:182:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:3011:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:6830:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:9259:  1469	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:3059:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7381:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1469:   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:3063:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7389:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:1677:   556	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-03/raw-output.txt:3107:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:7715:reviews/2026-07-18-goal-loop-plan/iteration-04/raw-output.txt:19077:   808	   348	    58	**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

2061:reviews/2026-07-18-loop-failover/test-verifier/iteration-02/raw-output.txt:4558:docs/plans/2026-07-11-baton-v1.md:58:**Concurrency** (Gate-1 additions, iterations 1+2): all bundle mutations run under a repo-scoped lock — `.handoff/lock` acquired via atomic `mkdir`/`O_EXCL`, containing `{writerId: <platform>-<pid>-<sessionHint>, fencingToken: <random per acquisition>, acquiredAt, heartbeatAt}`. **Lock model (iterations 3+4)**: mutation locks are **operation-scoped** — acquired for the duration of one command's mutation and released, never held across turns; logical session ownership lives in `bundle.json` (the active `origin`/generation), not in the lock. Lock metadata (host, pid, process start time, fencing token) is written atomically with acquisition; a crash between lock creation and metadata publication reads as torn metadata. Recovery rules, conservative on every OS: automatic recovery only when the owner is **provably dead** (same host, pid gone or pid/start-time mismatch); a same-host owner confirmed alive is **refused** — including `recover --force` — with the instruction to terminate that process first; missing/torn/cross-host/unverifiable owner metadata is treated as **unsupported for automatic recovery** (refusal with explanation), never as safe-to-steal. Fencing tokens remain a fast-abort layer. Tests: force attempted against a live paused writer (refused), crash between lock creation and metadata publication, owner paused after its final token check, torn-metadata refusal. Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

Journal entries carry `writerId`; sequence numbers are allocated under the lock. **Semantic isolation**: v1 enforces one active task — a checkpoint whose `sessionHint`/origin doesn't match the active bundle is rejected with an actionable warning (`--take-over` supersedes: archives the current bundle to `history/` and starts fresh), so two unrelated sessions can't merge goals/files/decisions into one handoff. `receive` is a core-owned two-phase transaction. `receive --prepare` validates + resolves roles + returns a one-time receipt token and the resume prompt without mutating state; the token **binds** the bundle revision (journalSeq), normalized intake, config digest, target platform+session, the probe snapshot used for remap, **and a content-sensitive prepare-time git digest** — HEAD + branch + hashes of the staged and unstaged diffs + a bounded untracked-files digest (path + size + content hash, capped) — so a file that stays `M` but changes content still invalidates the token. `--commit` re-derives and compares every bound input, rejecting any drift (intervening checkpoint, config edit, HEAD move, content change, probe change) and requiring re-prepare; each declared drift input has its own rejection test. `receive --commit <token>` performs one atomic transition: `sealed → received` (normal) or `open → received` (the primary failure case: limit death before finalize; commit writes a receive-generated degraded seal recording intake origin/reason, flagged `degraded-seal`) — and in the same transition **adopts the receiving platform/session as the bundle's active owner and opens a fresh writable generation** (`generation` counter incremented, `status: open`), archiving the prior seal + receipt to `history/`. The receiving session's subsequent checkpoints are therefore first-party, and the bundle is immediately receivable again if the new platform also dies — chained A→B→C failover is contract-tested with checkpoints fired immediately after each receive. Cancellation or a competing receiver leaves state untouched; double-commit fails cleanly. Identical semantics on every adapter; six-direction contract tests cover sealed + unsealed variants. Tests: concurrent writers, provably-dead takeover, fencing-token abort incl. pause-after-final-check, foreign-session rejection/take-over, prepare-vs-checkpoint races, prepare-without-commit, double-commit, competing receivers, chained failovers.

     1	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
     2	
     3	// Git facts degrade to null rather than block a checkpoint: not-a-repo,
     4	// missing binary, and timeouts are all expected environments (plan §Root
     5	// discovery & degraded modes).
     6	const GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
     7	// The untracked digest is bounded: beyond this many paths, entries fold in by
     8	// name only, keeping prepare-time hashing cheap on huge untracked trees.
     9	const UNTRACKED_CAP = 200;
    10	// NUL separator: cannot occur in diffs, sizes, hex hashes, or file paths, so
    11	// joined digest inputs cannot collide across field boundaries.
    12	const SEP = String.fromCharCode(0);
    13	const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
    14	
    15	const sha256 = (/** @type {string} */ s) => createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex');
    16	
    17	/**
    18	 * Capture the repo's git state plus a content-sensitive digest. The digest
    19	 * covers the staged diff, unstaged diff, and a bounded untracked-files digest
    20	 * (path + size + content hash) — NOT the HEAD sha, which the receive token
    21	 * binds as its own input, so a HEAD-only move is distinguishable from a
    22	 * content change.
    23	 * @param {{execFile: Function, cwd: string, fs: any}} deps
    24	 * @returns {Promise<{branch: string, headSha: string, dirty: boolean, dirtySummary: string[], contentDigest: string} | null>}
    25	 */
    26	export async function snapshot({ execFile, cwd, fs }) {
    27	  const git = (/** @type {string[]} */ args) => execFile('git', args, { cwd, timeout: GIT_TIMEOUT_MS });
    28	  let branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList;
    29	  try {
    30	    [branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList] = await Promise.all([
    31	      git(['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD']),
    32	      git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']),
    33	      git(['status', '--porcelain']),
    34	      git(['diff', '--cached']),
    35	      git(['diff']),
    36	      git(['ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard']),
    37	    ]);
    38	  } catch {
    39	    return null;
    40	  }
    41	
    42	  const nonEmptyLines = (/** @type {string} */ s) => s.split(NEWLINE).filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l !== '');
    43	  const dirtySummary = nonEmptyLines(status.stdout);
    44	  const untrackedPaths = nonEmptyLines(untrackedList.stdout);
    45	
    46	  const untrackedEntries = untrackedPaths.map((rel, i) => {
    47	    if (i >= UNTRACKED_CAP) return [rel, 'capped'].join(SEP);
    48	    try {
    49	      const content = fs.readFileSync(cwd + '/' + rel, 'utf8');
    50	      return [rel, String(Buffer.byteLength(content)), sha256(content)].join(SEP);
    51	    } catch {
    52	      // Listed but unreadable (deleted mid-flight): still digest its presence.
    53	      return [rel, 'absent'].join(SEP);
    54	    }
    55	  });
    56	
    57	  return {
    58	    branch: branch.stdout.trim(),
    59	    headSha: head.stdout.trim(),
    60	    dirty: dirtySummary.length > 0,
    61	    dirtySummary,
    62	    contentDigest: sha256([staged.stdout, unstaged.stdout, ...untrackedEntries].join(SEP)),
    63	  };
    64	}

  8907	    16

  8909	    18	 * Capture the repo's git state plus a content-sensitive digest. The digest
  8910	    19	 * covers the staged diff, unstaged diff, and a bounded untracked-files digest
  8911	    20	 * (path + size + content hash) — NOT the HEAD sha, which the receive token
  8912	    21	 * binds as its own input, so a HEAD-only move is distinguishable from a
  8913	    22	 * content change.
  8914	    23	 * @param {{execFile: Function, cwd: string, fs: any}} deps
  8915	    24	 * @returns {Promise<{branch: string, headSha: string, dirty: boolean, dirtySummary: string[], contentDigest: string} | null>}
  8916	    25	 */

  8934	    43	  const dirtySummary = nonEmptyLines(status.stdout);
  8935	    44	  const untrackedPaths = nonEmptyLines(untrackedList.stdout);

  3844	function gitExec(headForCall) {

  3846	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
  3847	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));

    26	//     prior limit death left the bundle unsealed). runFailover then SKIPS

    28	//     the receive generates a degraded seal). The default alive path checkpoints
    29	//     -> finalize (seals) -> sealed receive.

    33	//     relaunch  -> { action:'relaunch', class, assignment, avoidEntries?, prompt? }

    36	// (git rev-parse HEAD returning different values on successive calls) — the
    37	// production receive path re-derives git for prepare and for commit, so a HEAD
    38	// change between them stales the token. There is NO test-only hook.

   141	// A git execFile whose HEAD is chosen per rev-parse-HEAD call (the drift seam),
   142	// and which counts those calls so a test can pin the exact number of
   143	// prepare->commit windows. gitSnapshot reads clean status/diffs.
   144	function gitExec(headForCall) {
   145	  let headCalls = 0;
   146	  const fn = (/** @type {string} */ cmd, /** @type {string[]} */ args = []) => {
   147	    if (cmd !== 'git') return Promise.reject(Object.assign(new Error('spawn ENOENT'), { code: 'ENOENT' }));
   148	    const key = args.join(' ');
   149	    if (key === 'rev-parse HEAD') {
   150	      headCalls += 1;
   151	      return Promise.resolve({ stdout: headForCall(headCalls) + '\n', stderr: '' });
   152	    }
   153	    const out = key === 'rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD' ? 'main' : '';
   154	    return Promise.resolve({ stdout: out + '\n', stderr: '' });
   155	  };
   156	  fn.headCalls = () => headCalls;
   157	  return fn;
   158	}

   160	// Spy every write touching .handoff/loop.
   161	function spyLoopWrites(io) {
   162	  const writes = /** @type {string[]} */ ([]);
   163	  const note = (/** @type {any} */ p) => { if (typeof p === 'string' && p.startsWith('/repo/.handoff/loop')) writes.push(p); };
   164	  for (const m of ['writeFileSync', 'appendFileSync', 'mkdirSync', 'unlinkSync', 'rmSync']) {
   165	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   166	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ p, /** @type {any} */ a) => { note(p); return real(p, a); };
   167	  }
   168	  for (const m of ['renameSync', 'copyFileSync']) {
   169	    const real = io.fs[m].bind(io.fs);
   170	    io.fs[m] = (/** @type {any} */ from, /** @type {any} */ to) => { note(from); note(to); return real(from, to); };
   171	  }
   172	  return writes;
   173	}
